newsitem.title: CHINA: Yuan ends slightly up vs US dollar in Shanghai.
newsitem.headline: Yuan ends slightly up vs US dollar in Shanghai.

text.p: The Chinese yuan closed slightly up at 8.2928 on Tuesday from Monday's 8.2931 against the U.S. dollar in Shanghai and traders said sentiment was cautious.

China's strong foreign trade data for the January to May period announced last week supported the yuan's upward trend on Tuesday but fears over possible central bank's intervention to depress the yuan prevented it from rising solidly, they said.
The weighted average price on Monday was 8.2931.
The yuan opened lower at an intraday low of 8.2933 and moved around 8.2930 for most of the session, hitting a high of 8.2877 late in trading.
Trading was slow with most business done at 8.2929, traders said.
Official figures issued last Friday put China's foreign trade surplus for the first five months of the year at $13.95 billion against a deficit of $451 million for the same period last year.
One dealer said the yuan gained support from buyers who expected it to go up due to the strong foreign trade surplus.
But a second dealer said the People's Bank's intervention to depress the yuan in early June had made traders cautious.
"Selling due to cautious sentiment was seen between 8.2920 and 8.2925, limiting the yuan's upward momentum," he said.
Dealers said they expected the yuan to move around 8.2930 on Wednesday.
The yuan closed down slightly at 7.3189 from 7.3000 against 100 Japanese yen and lower at 1.0722 from 1.0709 against the Hong Kong dollar.
